pages.title: A Bigger Pocket
pages.text: Take your supplies along without filling every ordinary slot.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.text: Craft a basic backpack and inspect its upgrade slots. Install the rewarded pickup upgrade; merely carrying it will not complete its practical lesson.

pages.title: How to use it
pages.text: Use the bound backpack key or native placed-item interaction. Copper/iron/gold/diamond/netherite conversions expand storage/upgrade slots according to recipes while preserving contents.

pages.title: Useful to know
pages.text: In the recipe viewer, R shows recipes and U shows uses. Ctrl+F focuses search; @ filters a source, - excludes a term and quotes match a phrase. The + button transfers only available ingredients; Ctrl+O hides the list. For conflicting recipes use the result-selection button, also available for

pages.title: Useful to know
pages.text: Claim the quest reward, then open ordinary inventory: items wait in the separate take-only delivery panel. Collect individual stacks; leftovers persist when inventory is full. Nothing can be inserted. Claims are personal even with shared team progress.

pages.title: Useful to know
pages.text: The book has seven main tabs. Nearby paths usually suggest order without blocking an already available objective. Click a quest message to open it; item/guide pages help explain unfamiliar uses.

pages.title: Useful to know
pages.text: Click the underlined completed quest title in chat to open that exact quest. It navigates an already credited objective; it is not another requirement.

pages.title: Useful to know
pages.text: Crafting, building, farming, combat, trading and dimensions remain the survival backbone. Backports add some newer minecraft-namespaced items; installed owners and pack rules determine their availability.

pages.title: Useful to know
pages.text: Shared team completion and personal rewards differ. Members can help each other, but allies are not members and administrator teams are not ordinary parties. /smp and its parties exist only on dedicated hosts.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Use the inventory book icon, a supported quest-book item or a configured keybinding, then select a chapter. Authored quests show their description, tasks and rewards; a pack without quest definitions has an empty book.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Configure item, choice, random/loot-table, XP, command or stage rewards as supported by the installed branch. Choice selects an option; random/loot tables and command rewards have different result contracts.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Inspect an item task before collecting or crafting its target. ItemTask separates inventory checks from only_from_crafting progress, consuming submission and task_screen_only insertion; NBT and weak-NBT matching alter acceptable stacks. Owning an item cannot prove its use.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Click a permitted manual task button only when the task requests acknowledgment. The optional CustomTask button sends submission to the server; progress still needs its configured callback. An unconnected custom task is not automatically an action detector.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Complete the required prerequisite objects, then advance through sequential tasks if enabled. Quest supports all/any or minimum-count dependencies, started/completed requirements, hidden details and exclusive branches. Visibility and completion are distinct; optional/repeat settings do not imply

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Claim the rewards of a repeatable quest and observe its configured repeat gate. The native repeat path checks every reward claim; Quest exposes a separate repeat cooldown. A completed task is not proof that a player claimed the reward.
